items.title: George Russell — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Buckwheat was the bass player with this group... Buckwheat was fascinated. He fell in love with the . . . Concept... Buckwheat told Dave Guard about the Concept.

ctx.x: You were – the recording date itself was ’49. So you were pretty much well into, maybe in the middle of – you tell me. I don’t – but you were well into The Lydian, the formalizing of the concept at that point. Then you actually had it completed and got it published. When was that? Was that the early ’50s?

I have to think first where I got the money to publish it. That’s sort of an unbelievable – a hard to believe story that actually happened. A fellow named Buckwheat – his first name was actually – we called him Buckwheat, but his first name was – I don’t really remember that. But he was traveling with a group, very successful group of the day. Hmm. It was a pop group. They were at the top of . . .
A singing group? Gee, there’s so many groups. When I start thinking of that time frame, the Dominos and the Ink Spots. The Mills Brothers were older.
